bug_semantics: The html_to_markdown expansion accepted authenticated user-controlled HTTP(S) URLs and tried to block loopback, private, and link-local destinations. Its IP check parsed an IPv4-mapped IPv6 literal or DNS result as IPv6 and compared it directly with IPv4 blocked networks, so values such as ::ffff:127.0.0.1 and ::ffff:169.254.169.254 missed the corresponding IPv4 ranges and reached requests.get, enabling SSRF to internal services or instance metadata.
flaw_origin: Commit 52cda9caa003cafe87e14ae3721db5e16f6f111a first wrote the advisory-specific flawed guard: _is_ip_blocked passed ipaddress.ip_address(ip_str) directly to membership tests against IPv4 networks, and both literal and DNS-result paths used that helper. Its parent 89abdc6855c84084c2d412205c0deff6b82bc593 had the pre-existing unrestricted requests.get sink but none of these IP-filter lines; thus 52cda9caa003cafe87e14ae3721db5e16f6f111a is the atomic first-write BIC for the mapped-address protection bypass, not a move or revert.
ai_marker: No AI marker is present on the BIC. The complete commit object names David Cruciani <david.cruciani@circl.lu> as both author and committer, credits Bilal Teke as the reporter, has no Co-Authored-By or generator trailer, and the public commit page attributes this single-parent commit to DavidCruciani.
evidence: The published CVE-2026-62143 CNA record identifies MISP/misp-modules, describes the IPv4-mapped IPv6 normalization failure and SSRF impact, marks versions through v3.0.8 affected, and cites 3bae4108a3ba1e507727d5264697fd7303ba0b89 as the patch.

git show of 52cda9caa003cafe87e14ae3721db5e16f6f111a shows that it added BLOCKED_RANGES, _is_ip_blocked, hostname resolution checks, is_safe_url, and the guarded requests.get call; _is_ip_blocked compared the parsed address directly with the blocked networks without checking IPv6Address.ipv4_mapped.

git blame at direct-fix parent cc5ce935cae339d6f5f624e981762d65e1c2d1fa attributes the vulnerable range table, _is_ip_blocked, resolver path, and is_safe_url path to 52cda9caa003cafe87e14ae3721db5e16f6f111a. That BIC has exactly one parent, 89abdc6855c84084c2d412205c0deff6b82bc593.

A local stdlib reproduction shows ipaddress.ip_address('::ffff:127.0.0.1') is an IPv6Address that is not a member of IPv4 network 127.0.0.0/8, while its ipv4_mapped value 127.0.0.1 is a member, proving the guard's bypass and the normalization mechanism.

Commit 3bae4108a3ba1e507727d5264697fd7303ba0b89 introduces _normalize_ip_address, applies it before blocked-range membership tests, rejects URLs without a hostname, and adds literal and DNS-result regression tests for mapped loopback/private/link-local addresses. Follow-up ad2a0511c52449ad4fec97a30f4848f92676bed7 uses getattr for Python versions whose IPv4Address lacks ipv4_mapped; it does not change the advisory's mapped-IPv6 fix mechanism.

Tag ancestry matches the CNA release boundary: v3.0.8 contains 52cda9caa003cafe87e14ae3721db5e16f6f111a and does not contain 3bae4108a3ba1e507727d5264697fd7303ba0b89; v3.0.9 is the first observed release tag containing the direct fix and its compatibility follow-up.
The BIC's full author, committer, subject, body, and public GitHub commit page contain no AI-assistance marker; the only provenance credit is the human reporter line '- As reported by Bilal Teke'.

The immediate parent establishes the first-write boundary for the defective protection logic, while blame through the fix parent shows those lines survived until remediation.
